harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured secure, atomic synchronization from node1 to node2 every five minutes. An automatic test change synchronized in 38 seconds. Both nodes retained the installed RHEL 10.0 release and 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 kernel, and passed sequential restart/recovery validation.
actions_performed: Initialized the previously absent source file on node1 and destination on node2 with restricted permissions.
Created a dedicated locked SSH identity restricted to reading only the source file, with node1's host key pinned on node2.
Installed a hardened systemd service and persistent five-minute timer on node2; updates use atomic replacement and preserve the last good copy on failure.
Verified an automatic timer-driven change, then removed the test marker and restored both files to their original empty state.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities, services, data, connectivity, and post-restart synchronization.

evidence.requirement: node1 is the source of truth and node2 holds a matching copy
evidence.summary: Final source, destination, and live-pull SHA-256 values match: e3b0c442…; both files contain the restored original empty content.

evidence.requirement: Changes are picked up automatically within 15 minutes
evidence.summary: The source changed at 14:06:56 and the timer updated node2 at 14:07:34, an observed delay of 38 seconds.
The timer is enabled and active with OnUnitActiveSec=5min and Persistent=yes; it ran successfully automatically after node2 reboot.

evidence.requirement: Synchronization access and credentials are secured
evidence.summary: The dedicated account uses a forced read-only command, the server host key is pinned, the private key is root-only mode 0600, and an arbitrary remote command produced no command output.

evidence.requirement: Installed operating-system release and kernel were retained
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 before and after restart.
Healthy baseline boot ID 434803ac… was captured, restart acknowledged, boot ID changed to 25e33e92…, and system state, SSH, firewall, SELinux, source data, account, and cross-node reads recovered.

Healthy baseline boot ID 254597f8… was captured, restart acknowledged, boot ID changed to 1c7f2259…, and system state, security services, destination data, authentication, timer, and an automatic post-boot synchronization recovered.
